column1: # Re-dispatch of the full-width retention wave under a distinct basename, because the first
# dispatch named a code snapshot frozen before --keep-full-features existed and its cells were
# refused by argparse with exit 2. The snapshot used here carries the flag and is otherwise
# identical to the primary extraction on the measured path: the only difference in
# extract_stability_singles.py is the flag, its help text and the branch that writes the
# unprojected per-state blocks to a separate file.
# D1 stability gate: full-width state retention pass over the same frozen 101-background
# single-mutant cohort and the same label-free plan as the primary extraction (content
# digest 283b4503ea166a3d61052bf68818c8aef162692ed3eb436a7a9864759a48763d). Identical measurement identity, identical sequences, identical batch-one
# setting; the only difference is --keep-full-features, which writes the unprojected
# per-state block outputs beside the projected ones.
# It exists so that the pending readout-class reassessment can refit a different projection
# or a different readout head on these frozen states without a second forward pass. The
# primary results are read from the projected blocks of the primary pass and do not depend
# on this pass. Lanes are ordered residue-level and byte-level arms first, because a
# representation claim about protein stability would be read on those.
